alignments.note: כִּי takes the *For* written for it.
Prepositional predicate of a verbless clause takes the construction-supplied copula on the preposition (rule 49); discontinuous around the negative under rule 25.
Subject noun keeps only its own word, the copula having gone to the predicate (rule 20).
The אִם opening this rhetorical question takes the fronted auxiliary *doth* (rule 17).
Prepositional predicate; *endure* is a linking verb written where a copula would stand and joins this preposition's unit (rules 20, 49), headed on the word carrying the relation.
The repeated דּוֹר וָדוֹר is rendered once by a plural with a supplied *all*, which determines the nominal expression under rule 15.
The ASV writes no *and* inside *all generations* (rule 14).
The repeated occurrence the ASV renders only once is its own unrepresented unit (rule 22).

review_notes: Competing reading for s010/s012: giving *generations* to the second דּוֹר on rule 22's tail-to-tail reading; that reading governs counted nouns distributed across numerals, and this is a distributive repetition, so the first occurrence is taken as the rendered one.

Competing reading for t011: marking *endure* added as a supplied lexical verb under rule 20; taken as a linking verb because a prepositional predicate morpheme stands in the clause for it and dropping the word removes only the link, not a predication the Hebrew never wrote.
